item.content:encoded:
Well I never gave much thought to where Geoff is from. I'm sorry you feel that it draws from the humour, but I didn't consider it at all relevant to the joke. I, myself, am English, so that's where most of the phrasing is from.

As for the fronts, the joke is that they were clearly named by someone who wasn't very good at coming up with inconspicuous names, since both names have the initials "SCP" and the second contains the word "Protocols", making it sound more like a secret government installation than a carpentry shop. I see where you're coming from, when you say that everything except Geoff should be deadly serious, but I disagree. Also, I'm really not sure what you mean when you say "Nobody is called 'Stephany'" because it's a fairly common name.

Anyway, thanks for the feedback! Much appreciated.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I very much like the idea but there are some false notes in the execution that are spoiling it for me. It might be pure pedantry but for what it's worth:

Where is Geoff from? The 'alright mate' might be Britain or Australia, as is the talk of 'gents'. (The SCP soldier's 'FLAMING CHRIST' is also extremely Aussie.) But then we have a US note in 'Hey man!' and 'I've kinda gotta pee' from Geoff and I don't quite know what he sounds like, which bothers me slightly. If the SCP guys are all gung-ho US Marines types dealing with Nameless Horrors and Geoff is an oblivious, genial UK or Aussie everyman dealing with day-to-day stuff, that's the funny contrast that is at the heart of the gag. A clear voice really helps with that but it's rather muddy at the moment.

If I can be amazingly pretentious about joke format for a minute, I don't like the SCP front names very much, because nobody is called 'Stephany' and a carpentry shop with 'Protocols' in the name isn't very believable either. If the gag is structured around the contrast between everyman Geoff and the established, canonical tone of the SCP project, then I think the latter has to be the control group in the experiment: the SCP aspects of the joke need to be unchanged, and Geoff, the anomaly, introduced. So the SCP front names need to be as plausible as SCP front names are in non-joke skips, is what I mean.
